ai.definition: Room-temperature superconductors are materials that theoretically conduct electricity with zero electrical resistance at or near ambient temperature (room temperature) and normal atmospheric pressure.
ai.howItWorks: Theoretical room-temperature superconductors would operate by allowing electrons to flow without any energy loss, which is currently only observed in certain materials at extremely low temperatures. Researchers use computational methods to predict potential superconducting materials, followed by experimental synthesis under high pressures to observe the material's properties.
ai.problemSolved: Eliminating electrical losses in power transmission and enabling efficient magnetic applications such as maglev trains and MRI machines without cooling requirements.
ai.manufacturing: Current manufacturing processes involve computationally predicting candidate materials, synthesizing them under high pressure, and then testing for superconductivity. This is a complex process that requires specialized equipment and expertise.
ai.buildProcess: The build process begins with computational modeling to identify potential superconducting compounds, followed by the synthesis of these compounds under high-pressure conditions using diamond anvil cells or other methods. The synthesized materials are then tested for their electrical resistance at various temperatures and pressures.
ai.costDrivers: High costs associated with specialized equipment, such as diamond anvil cells, which can cost hundreds of thousands of dollars each. Additionally, the need for highly skilled researchers and engineers to perform computational predictions and experimental synthesis drives up labor costs.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook remains uncertain due to repeated claims of breakthroughs that have not been reproducibly verified in peer-reviewed literature or by independent research groups. While the potential benefits are significant, practical implementation is still far from reality.
ai.regulation: No specific regulations currently exist for room-temperature superconductors as they remain theoretical and unproven at ambient conditions. However, any future developments could require regulatory oversight related to safety, environmental impact, and energy infrastructure.
ai.risks: The primary risk is the potential for false claims or premature announcements that do not hold up under rigorous scientific scrutiny. This can lead to wasted resources and misallocation of research funding.
ai.profitability: Currently, no profitability as room-temperature superconductors are unproven at ambient conditions. However, if realized, they could revolutionize industries such as power transmission and magnetic technology, potentially leading to significant economic benefits.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future development will likely involve advancements in computational materials science, improvements in high-pressure synthesis techniques, and the discovery of new superconducting compounds through both theoretical predictions and experimental validation.

glossary.def: A material that exhibits zero electrical resistance at or near ambient temperature (room temperature) and normal atmospheric pressure.
The use of computer simulations to predict the properties of materials before they are synthesized, often used in materials science research.
A device used to create high-pressure environments for synthesizing and testing superconducting materials under extreme conditions.

buildSteps.title: Predict candidate structures
buildSteps.detail: Computationally screen hydrogen-rich hydrides and layered compounds for strong electron–phonon coupling or other pairing mechanisms.

buildSteps.title: Synthesise under pressure
buildSteps.detail: Load the elements into a diamond anvil cell and laser-heat them to form new phases at pressures of tens to hundreds of gigapascals.

buildSteps.title: Measure for superconductivity
buildSteps.detail: Look for a drop to zero electrical resistance and expulsion of a magnetic field (Meissner effect) as the sample cools.

buildSteps.title: Confirm structure and composition
buildSteps.detail: Use X-ray diffraction and spectroscopy to identify which phase is responsible for the signal.

buildSteps.title: Attempt ambient-pressure stabilisation
buildSteps.detail: Try chemical pressure, strain, intercalation or thin-film epitaxy to keep the structure stable at zero pressure.

buildSteps.title: Scale up synthesis
buildSteps.detail: Grow bulk samples or films by routes that can be replicated outside tiny high-pressure cells.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate a conductor
buildSteps.detail: Pattern or draw the material into wires or tapes with low-resistance contacts.

buildSteps.title: Test application metrics
buildSteps.detail: Measure critical temperature, critical current density and upper critical field at usable temperatures and fields.

prerequisites.why: BCS and Eliashberg theory work for simple metals but not reliably for hydrides or unconventional pairings.
diamond anvil cells reach hundreds of gigapascals, but samples are microscopic.
no known method keeps high-pressure superconducting phases stable at zero pressure.
thin films and some bulk ceramics exist, but not for hydride superconductors.
needed to characterise materials and to operate today's superconductors; a true room-temperature material would remove this need.

pathway.milestone: high-pressure hydride superconductors reach temperatures above 200 K, but only under roughly 100–200 GPa and in microscopic samples
pathway.unlocks: a proving ground for pairing theory and high-temperature superconductivity.

pathway.milestone: independent replication or refutation of ambient-pressure claims, plus a clearer picture of the pairing mechanism
pathway.unlocks: reliable guidance for which structures to pursue.

pathway.milestone: stabilise one known high-temperature phase at ambient pressure using strain, chemical pressure or thin-film engineering
pathway.unlocks: a material that can be handled and measured without a pressure cell.

pathway.milestone: demonstrate a wire or film carrying useful current at room temperature in a magnetic field
commercial lossless grids, compact magnets and maglev
pathway.unlocks: large cuts in electrical losses and new electromagnetic devices, if bulk manufacture becomes cheap.
